newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end sharply higher on Wall Street rally.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end sharply higher on Wall Street rally.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks posted their biggest point gain in more than two months on Wednesday after U.S. economic data calmed fears about higher interest rates and triggered an overnight surge on Wall Street, brokers said.
"Confidence has been boosted by the Dow overnight and also the long bond," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.

The blue chip Hang Seng index jumped 302.88 points, or 2.40 percent, to close at 12,903.30, just slightly off the day's high of 12,924.27. Turnover rose to HK$13.82 billion from HK$11.03 billion on Tuesday.

Weaker-than-expected data on U.S. wage inflation and orders for manufactured goods propelled the Dow industrials to their second-largest point rise ever on Tuesday, up 179.01 points, or 2.64 percent, to 6,962.03.
The U.S. long bond jumped 1-17/32 to yield 6.98 percent, under seven percent, which brokers said indicated that chances for an imminent interest rate rise were limited.
"The interest rate rise pressure is seen smaller and we believe the possibility for a rise in May is not big now," said Stanley Ng, research manager at Mansion House Research.

Sentiment was further lifted by the encouraging earnings announced by HSBC Holding's American arm, brokers said. HSBC Americans Inc's a net income rose 33 pecent in the first quarter this year to US$114.54 million.
"Probably figures from HSBC Americas, which came in overnight, are the reason the market is taking an opportunity to buy or bargain-hunt on HSBC," Remington said.
HSBC, the most heavily traded stock of the session, jumped to a record high of HK$196.50 before retreating slightly to close up HK$6.00 at HK$196.00.
Among interest rate sensitive stocks, banks led the gainers with Hang Seng Bank rising HK$2.50 to HK$87.25 and Bank of East Asia up HK$0.50 to HK$26.65.
Sun Hung Kai Properties jumped HK$3.25 to HK$84.00 and New World Development soared HK$1.80 to HK$44.70.
Red-chips and H-shares also recovered from a two-day consolidation with CITIC Pacific adding HK$1.00 to HK$41.90 and China Merchants up HK$0.40 to HK$8.30.
The H-share index jumped 27.52 points to 1,067.45.
May Hang Seng Index futures rose 280 points to 12,820.
